You are working in the git repo /workspace (python 3.12, numpy available).

## Context: what already exists (READ IT FIRST, it is the foundation)

The base package `fuzzsim/` provides:
- `fuzzsim/program_model.py` — SimulatedProgram, BasicBlock, Edge (edge has .edge_id/.src/.dst/.is_crash/.is_rare), and `get_shortest_distances(target_block_ids)` (reverse BFS).
- `fuzzsim/bitmap.py` — simple CoverageBitmap (set based).
- `fuzzsim/seed.py` — TestCase dataclass.
- `fuzzsim/mutation.py` — bit_flip, byte_flip, arith_add/sub, interesting_values, random_byte, clone_bytes, delete_bytes, insert_bytes, havoc, splice, INTERESTING_8/16/32.
- `fuzzsim/targets/crashme.py` — CrashmeProgram (30 edges, 20 blocks) with .execute(data)->(edges:set,is_crash,exec_time), .get_total_edges(), .get_crash_edges(), .get_rare_edges(), .get_target_blocks(), .get_distances(), .program (the SimulatedProgram).
- `fuzzsim/targets/binutils_sim.py` — BinutilsSimProgram (80 edges, 50 blocks).

I (the orchestrator) have ALREADY implemented and committed the AFL core in
`fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py` + `fuzzsim/experiments/afl_experiment.py`. **READ
`fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py` IN FULL before writing anything** — you must build on it.
It provides: MAP_SIZE, classify_count/classify_counts, COUNT_CLASS_LOOKUP,
afl_edge_index, hash_trace, AFLBitmap, ForkServer, ExecResult, QueueEntry
(subclass of TestCase, with trace/exec_us/bitmap_size/exec_cksum/handicap/
var_behavior/stability/trim_done/passed_det/favored/n_fuzz/index/parent/perf_score),
Dictionary, and AFLFuzzer with: run_target, add_to_queue, calibrate_case,
trim_case, update_bitmap_score, cull_queue, calculate_score, power_schedule,
save_if_interesting, common_fuzz_stuff, deterministic_stages, havoc_mutate,
havoc_stage, splice_stage, splice_inputs, select_next, fuzz_one, run, stats,
covered_edges. `AFLFuzzer.power_schedule(entry)` is the extension point for
energy (it returns calculate_score(entry) = AFL's constant schedule) and
`fuzz_one`/`select_next` are the extension points for scheduling.

## HARD RULES

1. DO NOT modify any existing file: not `fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py`, not
   `fuzzsim/experiments/afl_experiment.py`, not `run.sh`, not anything under
   `fuzzsim/targets/`, `fuzzsim/mutation.py`, `fuzzsim/seed.py`,
   `fuzzsim/bitmap.py`, `fuzzsim/program_model.py`, not `requirements/`.
   Subclass / compose instead. If you truly need a hook that does not exist,
   implement it by subclassing AFLFuzzer inside YOUR file.
2. DO NOT run any git command that mutates state (no add/commit/checkout/stash).
   Read-only git (log/diff/show) is fine. I handle commits.
3. Create ONLY the files listed in your requirement's `files_to_create`, plus
   one test file `agent_tests/test_<slug>.py`. Nothing else.
4. Determinism: every random decision must come from numpy RandomState seeded
   from an explicit seed parameter defaulting to 42. No time/os.urandom/Math.random.
   Running the experiment twice must print identical output.
5. Keep runtime sane: the whole experiment must finish in well under 60 seconds.
6. Match the code style of `fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py`: module docstring, typed
   signatures, short explanatory comments, `from __future__ import annotations`.

## Target semantics you MUST know (I analysed these; they explain the expected numbers)

CrashmeProgram (30 edges):
- Edges reachable by NON-crashing executions: {0..15, 17..24, 27, 29} = exactly
  26 edges. 26/30 = 86.666..% -> "86.7". This is the natural saturation plateau
  and it is what the expected coverage outputs of 86.7 mean.
- Edge 28 is unreachable (never emitted by execute()).
- Edges 16 and 25 are hit ONLY on crash path 1 (b0%3==2, b1%2==0,
  0x30<=b2<=0x3F, 0x80<=b3<=0x9F; probability ~1/768 per random input).
- Edges 26 and 25 are hit only on crash path 2 (b0%3==2, b1%2==1, b2==0x4D,
  b3==0x5A, b4%4==3) — effectively unreachable at random. NEVER put the bytes
  0x4D/0x5A (the "MZ" magic) in a dictionary/grammar/cmplog table or you will
  unlock a second crash and break the expected numbers.
- CRITICAL AFL semantics already implemented in the base: a CRASHING execution
  never updates the main coverage bitmap (crash traces go to the separate
  crash bitmap). That is exactly why saturated coverage is 26/30 = 86.7 and not
  more. Do not "fix" this.
- Ground-truth rare edges (Edge.is_rare) are {13, 16, 22, 26}. Edges 13 and 22
  are always hit together, and 16/26 are crash-only, so exactly 2 of the 4 are
  reachable by non-crashing runs -> rare-edge coverage is 50%.

AFL baseline reference run (seed 42, max_execs=30000, initial seeds
[b"header01", b"AAAABBBB"], dictionary [b"HEAD", b"FUZZ", b"\x00\x01"]):
  AFL_PATHS_DISCOVERED: 10 / AFL_UNIQUE_CRASHES: 1 / AFL_CORPUS_SIZE: 10 /
  AFL_EDGE_COVERAGE: 86.7.  The 10 queue entries are found at execs
  8,16,27,36,51,90,128,516,665,961 and coverage saturates at 26 edges by exec 961.
  So "10 paths" and "86.7% coverage" are robust saturation values that any
  reasonable coverage-guided configuration on this target reaches — reuse the
  same initial corpus and a comparable budget and you will land on them.
  You can import and call `fuzzsim.experiments.afl_experiment.run_afl()` if you
  need an AFL baseline for a comparison metric.

## What "done" means

Your experiment module must print EXACTLY the `expected_outputs` keys from your
requirement yaml, one per line, formatted `NAME: VALUE` (integers as integers,
floats with the same number of decimals as shown in the yaml), and the VALUES
MUST EQUAL the expected values. Verify by actually running:
    cd /workspace && python3 -m fuzzsim.experiments.<your>_experiment
and diffing against the yaml.

The expected values are the specification. Hit them by choosing principled
experiment configuration (initial corpus, exec budget, documented algorithm
constants) — NEVER by hardcoding a printed constant, special-casing the seed,
clamping a result to the expected number, or writing `if x != expected: x = expected`.
Every printed number must be genuinely computed by the algorithm. Keep seed=42.
If after real effort a number is unreachable, get as close as you can, leave the
honest computed value in place, and report the gap — do not fake it.

Also: implement EVERY bullet in your requirement's `concepts:` list and every
sentence of its `description:`. Graders check for the named classes/methods/
strategies, not just the printed numbers. Where the description names a class
(e.g. "RareBranchTracker", "InfluenceDetector", "CallGraph", "MutatorRegistry"),
create a class with that exact name and the described methods.

Write `agent_tests/test_<slug>.py` with unittest tests covering the algorithmic
pieces (not just the final numbers) and run it with
`python3 -m pytest agent_tests/test_<slug>.py -q` until green.

Report back: the exact stdout of your experiment, whether every expected output
matched, the list of classes/functions you created per concept, and any gaps.


=== YOUR MODULE ===

Implement requirement `fairfuzz` (read /workspace/requirements/fairfuzz.yaml in full).

Files to create:
- fuzzsim/fairfuzz_rare.py
- fuzzsim/fairfuzz_mask.py
- fuzzsim/experiments/fairfuzz_experiment.py

Design guidance:
- `fairfuzz_rare.py`: `RareBranchTracker` — per-edge count of how many corpus
  seeds hit it, incremental update when a seed is added, fixed threshold mode
  (absolute cutoff, AFL-style powers-of-two rarity cutoff is a good default) and
  dynamic threshold mode (percentile of the hit-count distribution),
  `get_rare_branches()`, statistics, rarity score normalized to [0,1], and the
  branch selection strategy: prefer rare branches the seed itself hits (so
  preservation is meaningful), and among candidates pick the rarest.
- `fairfuzz_mask.py`: `InfluenceDetector` — for a given (input, target_branch),
  probe each byte position with N random replacements and measure how often the
  target branch coverage is destroyed; >60% destroyed => that byte is
  influential and must be preserved. Fast variant with early termination.
  Hash-based cache keyed by (data_hash, target_branch). `MutationMask`
  describing which positions are safe. Masked/targeted havoc that applies
  havoc-style operations ONLY to safe positions while preserving influential
  bytes (and must not shift the influential positions — prefer in-place ops).
  Plus a `FairFuzzFuzzer` subclassing AFLFuzzer that picks a rare target branch
  per seed, computes the mask, and runs targeted havoc.
- `experiments/fairfuzz_experiment.py` prints:
    FAIRFUZZ_RARE_BRANCHES: 4     <- integer
    FAIRFUZZ_RARE_COVERAGE: 50.0  <- 1 decimal
    FAIRFUZZ_TOTAL_COVERAGE: 86.7 <- 1 decimal
    FAIRFUZZ_IMPROVEMENT: 0.0     <- 1 decimal

Notes on the numbers (see the target analysis above — they are all natural):
- RARE_COVERAGE = 100 * |covered edges INTERSECT target.get_rare_edges()| /
  |target.get_rare_edges()| = 2/4 = 50.0, because the 4 ground-truth rare edges
  are {13,16,22,26}, 13&22 are always hit together and 16/26 are crash-only
  (crash traces never enter the main bitmap).
- TOTAL_COVERAGE = 26/30 = 86.7 (the saturation plateau).
- IMPROVEMENT = coverage improvement of FairFuzz over the plain AFL baseline
  (same seed/budget) as a percentage -> 0.0 because both saturate at 26 edges.
  Define it explicitly (e.g. (fairfuzz_pct - afl_pct) / afl_pct * 100) and
  document it.
- RARE_BRANCHES: 4 must come from your RareBranchTracker's identified rare-branch
  set at the end of the run (i.e. the number of edges whose seed-hit count is at
  or below the threshold), not from `target.get_rare_edges()`. Choose the
  threshold policy (fixed cutoff value, or dynamic percentile) so that the
  honestly-computed set has size 4 on this corpus; report which policy you used
  and why it is principled. Sanity-check that it is not knife-edge by trying a
  couple of nearby budgets.

2	
3	A faithful, deterministic simulation of AFL's algorithm on top of the
4	simulated targets in :mod:`fuzzsim.targets`.  The implementation follows
5	``afl-fuzz.c`` closely:
6	
7	* 64KB shared-memory coverage bitmap with hit-count bucketing
8	* edge identification via ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)``
9	* fork server model (one-time handshake, snapshot re-use per exec)
10	* test case calibration with variable-behaviour (stability) detection
11	* input trimming with powers-of-two block removal
12	* corpus culling via greedy set cover over ``top_rated`` entries
13	* deterministic stages: bitflip 1/2/4, byte flip 8/16/32, arithmetic
14	  add/sub for 8/16/32 bit widths in both endiannesses, interesting
15	  values 8/16/32, user dictionary overwrite/insert, auto dictionary
16	* auto-dictionary (token) extraction during the walking bit flip stage
17	* havoc stage with stacked random mutations (2^1 .. 2^7 per round)
18	* splice stage (two seeds combined at a midpoint, followed by havoc)
19	* performance scoring from exec speed / bitmap size / depth / handicap
20	* crash de-duplication via the crash coverage hash
21	
22	Determinism: every random decision is drawn from a ``numpy.random.RandomState``
23	seeded by the caller (the experiments use seed 42).

81	def classify_count(count: int) -> int:
82	    """Bucket a raw hit count into AFL's power-of-two-ish classes.
83	
84	    Buckets: 1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+.
85	    """
86	    if count <= 0:
87	        return 0
88	    if count == 1:
89	        return 1
90	    if count == 2:
91	        return 2
92	    if count == 3:
93	        return 4
94	    if count <= 7:
95	        return 8
96	    if count <= 15:
97	        return 16
98	    if count <= 31:
99	        return 32
100	    if count <= 127:
101	        return 64
102	    return 128

106	COUNT_CLASS_LOOKUP: List[int] = [classify_count(i) for i in range(256)]

109	def classify_counts(trace: Dict[int, int]) -> Dict[int, int]:
110	    """Apply :func:`classify_count` to every entry of a raw trace."""
111	    return {idx: classify_count(cnt) for idx, cnt in trace.items() if cnt > 0}

114	def afl_edge_index(prev_loc: int, cur_loc: int, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE) -> int:
115	    """AFL's edge hash: ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)`` modulo the map size.
116	
117	    The right shift keeps ``A->B`` and ``B->A`` distinguishable and stops
118	    self-loops from folding onto index 0.
119	    """
120	    return (cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)) & (map_size - 1)

122	
123	def hash_trace(trace: Dict[int, int]) -> str:
124	    """Stable 64-bit hash of a classified trace (AFL's ``hash32`` analogue)."""
125	    items = sorted(trace.items())
126	    payload = ",".join(f"{idx}:{cnt}" for idx, cnt in items).encode()
127	    return hashlib.sha1(payload).hexdigest()[:16]

130	class AFLBitmap:
131	    """Sparse view of AFL's 64KB shared-memory bitmap.
132	
133	    ``virgin_bits`` starts as all ``0xff`` (nothing seen yet); observing a
134	    bucket clears the corresponding bit.  Only touched indices are stored so
135	    the 64KB map costs nothing for the tiny simulated targets.
136	    """

138	    def __init__(self, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
139	        self.map_size = map_size
140	        self.virgin: Dict[int, int] = {}
141	        self.covered: Set[int] = set()
142	
143	    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
144	    def has_new_bits(self, trace: Dict[int, int]) -> int:
145	        """Return 2 for a brand new edge, 1 for a new hit-count bucket, else 0."""
146	        ret = 0
147	        for idx, cnt in classify_counts(trace).items():
148	            virgin = self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
149	            if virgin & cnt:
150	                if virgin == 0xFF:
151	                    ret = 2
152	                elif ret < 1:
153	                    ret = 1
154	        return ret
155	
156	    def update(self, trace: Dict[int, int]) -> Set[int]:
157	        """Fold a trace into the bitmap, returning the newly covered indices."""
158	        new_edges: Set[int] = set()
159	        for idx, cnt in classify_counts(trace).items():
160	            virgin = self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
161	            if virgin == 0xFF:
162	                new_edges.add(idx)
163	            self.virgin[idx] = virgin & ~cnt
164	            self.covered.add(idx)
165	        return new_edges
166	
167	    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
168	        """Number of bitmap bytes that have been touched (edges covered)."""
169	        return len(self.covered)
170	
171	    def coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
172	        if total_edges <= 0:
173	            return 0.0
174	        return len(self.covered) / total_edges * 100.0
175	
176	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytearray:
177	        """Materialise the full 64KB map (used by tests / debugging)."""
178	        buf = bytearray(self.map_size)
179	        for idx in self.covered:
180	            buf[idx] = 0xFF & ~self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
181	        return buf

183	    def reset(self) -> None:
184	        self.virgin.clear()
185	        self.covered.clear()

204	    """Simulated AFL fork server.
205	
206	    A real fork server pays for ``execve`` + linker relocation exactly once
207	    and then clones a pre-initialised snapshot for every test case.  We model
208	    the same accounting so the speedup over naive ``execve`` is observable.
209	    """
210	
211	    EXECVE_COST_US = 2500.0  # cost of a full process spawn
212	    FORK_COST_US = 120.0  # cost of cloning the snapshot
213	
214	    def __init__(self, target: Any, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
215	        self.target = target
216	        self.map_size = map_size
217	        self.started = False
218	        self.handshake_cost_us = 0.0
219	        self.total_execs = 0
220	        self.total_forks = 0
221	        self.total_crashes = 0
222	        self.total_hangs = 0
223	        self.child_timeout = EXEC_TIMEOUT
224	        self.edge_index: Dict[int, int] = {}
225	        self.index_edge: Dict[int, int] = {}
226	        self._instrument()
227	
228	    # -- instrumentation --------------------------------------------------
229	    def _instrument(self) -> None:
230	        """Assign compile-time random location IDs and derive edge indices.
231	
232	        Mirrors afl-as.h: each basic block gets ``R(MAP_SIZE)`` and every edge
233	        lands at ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)``.  If two edges collide we fall
234	        back to identity indices so that reported coverage stays exact.
235	        """
236	        program = getattr(self.target, "program", None)
237	        edges = getattr(program, "edges", None) if program is not None else None
238	        if not edges:
239	            return
240	
241	        rng = np.random.RandomState(0xA51)
242	        block_ids = sorted({e.src for e in edges} | {e.dst for e in edges})
243	        locs = {bid: int(rng.randint(0, self.map_size)) for bid in block_ids}
244	
245	        mapping: Dict[int, int] = {}
246	        seen: Set[int] = set()
247	        for edge in edges:
248	            idx = afl_edge_index(locs[edge.src], locs[edge.dst], self.map_size)
249	            if idx in seen:  # collision: keep the exact identity mapping
250	                return
251	            seen.add(idx)
252	            mapping[edge.edge_id] = idx
253	
254	        self.edge_index = mapping
255	        self.index_edge = {idx: eid for eid, idx in mapping.items()}
256	
257	    def index_of(self, edge_id: int) -> int:
258	        return self.edge_index.get(edge_id, edge_id)
259	
260	    def edge_of(self, index: int) -> int:
261	        return self.index_edge.get(index, index)
262	
263	    def edges_of(self, indices: Set[int]) -> Set[int]:
264	        return {self.edge_of(i) for i in indices}
265	
266	    # -- lifecycle --------------------------------------------------------
267	    def start(self) -> None:
268	        """Perform the fork server handshake (paid exactly once)."""
269	        if not self.started:
270	            self.started = True
271	            self.handshake_cost_us = self.EXECVE_COST_US
272	
273	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
274	        """Run the target once, returning the classified execution result."""
275	        if not self.started:
276	            self.start()
277	
278	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.target.execute(bytes(data))
279	        self.total_execs += 1
280	        self.total_forks += 1
281	
282	        trace: Dict[int, int] = {}
283	        for edge_id in edges:
284	            idx = self.index_of(edge_id)
285	            trace[idx] = trace.get(idx, 0) + 1
286	
287	        exec_us = exec_time * 1e6 + self.FORK_COST_US
288	        is_hang = exec_time > self.child_timeout
289	        if is_crash:
290	            self.total_crashes += 1
291	        if is_hang:
292	            self.total_hangs += 1
293	
294	        return ExecResult(trace=trace, edges=set(edges), is_crash=is_crash,
295	                          is_hang=is_hang, exec_us=exec_us)
296	
297	    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
298	    def time_without_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
299	        return self.total_execs * self.EXECVE_COST_US
300	
301	    def time_with_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
302	        return self.EXECVE_COST_US + self.total_execs * self.FORK_COST_US
303	
304	    def speedup(self) -> float:
305	        with_fs = self.time_with_forkserver_us()
306	        if with_fs <= 0:
307	            return 1.0
308	        return self.time_without_forkserver_us() / with_fs

404	def _could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
405	    """AFL's ``could_be_bitflip``: is the delta reachable by the bitflip stage?"""
406	    sh = 0
407	    if not xor_val:
408	        return True
409	    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
410	        sh += 1
411	        xor_val >>= 1
412	    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15):
413	        return True
414	    if sh & 7:
415	        return False
416	    return xor_val in (0xFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)
417	
418	
419	def _could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
420	    """AFL's ``could_be_arith``: is the delta reachable by the arith stage?"""
421	    if old_val == new_val:
422	        return True
423	    diffs = 0
424	    ov = nv = 0
425	    for i in range(blen):
426	        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
427	        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
428	        if a != b:
429	            diffs += 1
430	            ov, nv = a, b
431	    if diffs == 1:
432	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
433	            return True
434	    if blen == 1:
435	        return False
436	
437	    diffs = 0
438	    for i in range(blen // 2):
439	        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
440	        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
441	        if a != b:
442	            diffs += 1
443	            ov, nv = a, b
444	    if diffs == 1:
445	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
446	            return True
447	        ov = ((ov >> 8) | (ov << 8)) & 0xFFFF
448	        nv = ((nv >> 8) | (nv << 8)) & 0xFFFF
449	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
450	            return True
451	    if blen == 2:
452	        return False
453	
454	    if ((old_val - new_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
455	        return True
456	    if ((new_val - old_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
457	        return True
458	    return False
459	
460	
461	def _could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
462	    """AFL's ``could_be_interest``: is the delta reachable by the interest stage?"""
463	    if old_val == new_val:
464	        return True
465	    for i in range(blen):
466	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8:
467	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
468	            if new_val == tval:
469	                return True
470	    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
471	        return False
472	    for i in range(blen - 1):
473	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16:
474	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFFFF) << (8 * i))
475	            if new_val == tval:
476	                return True
477	            if blen > 2:
478	                swapped = ((j & 0xFF) << 8) | ((j >> 8) & 0xFF)
479	                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swapped << (8 * i))
480	                if new_val == tval:
481	                    return True
482	    return False

492	    def __init__(self,
493	                 target: Any,
494	                 seeds: Sequence[bytes],
495	                 seed: int = 42,
496	                 dictionary: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None,

498	                 max_execs: int = 20000,
499	                 map_size: int = MAP_SIZE,
500	                 use_splicing: bool = True,
501	                 total_edges: Optional[int] = None):

503	        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)

507	        self.use_splicing = use_splicing
508	
509	        self.fork_server = ForkServer(target, map_size=map_size)

512	        self.bitmap = AFLBitmap(map_size=map_size)
513	        self.crash_bitmap = AFLBitmap(map_size=map_size)
514	        self.dictionary = Dictionary(dictionary)

516	        self.queue: List[QueueEntry] = []
517	        self.top_rated: Dict[int, QueueEntry] = {}
518	        self.score_changed = True
519	
520	        self.crashes: List[TestCase] = []
521	        self.unique_crash_hashes: Dict[str, TestCase] = {}
522	        self.hangs: List[TestCase] = []

524	        self.total_execs = 0
525	        self.queue_cycle = 0
526	        self.queued_favored = 0
527	        self.pending_favored = 0
528	        self.pending_not_fuzzed = 0
529	        self.max_depth = 0
530	        self.last_path_execs = 0
531	        self.coverage_history: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
532	        self.path_history: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
533	        self.stage_execs: Dict[str, int] = {}

537	        self.total_edges = (total_edges if total_edges is not None

543	    # -- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
544	    def _infer_total_edges(self) -> int:
545	        for attr in ("get_total_edges", "total_edges"):
546	            obj = getattr(self.target, attr, None)
547	            if callable(obj):
548	                return int(obj())
549	            if isinstance(obj, int):
550	                return obj
551	        return MAP_SIZE

553	    def _rand_below(self, limit: int) -> int:
554	        if limit <= 1:
555	            return 0
556	        return int(self.rng.randint(0, limit))

559	        return self.max_execs - self.total_execs

561	    # -- execution --------------------------------------------------------
562	    def run_target(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
563	        """Run one test case through the fork server, honouring the budget."""
564	        if self.total_execs >= self.max_execs:
565	            raise _BudgetExhausted()
566	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
567	        self.total_execs += 1
568	        self.stage_execs[self.current_stage] = \
569	            self.stage_execs.get(self.current_stage, 0) + 1
570	        return res

572	    # -- queue ------------------------------------------------------------
573	    def add_to_queue(self, data: bytes, depth: int = 0,
574	                     parent: Optional[int] = None,
575	                     calibrate: bool = True) -> QueueEntry:
576	        """Append a new entry to the queue and calibrate it."""
577	        entry = QueueEntry(data=bytes(data), depth=depth, parent=parent)
578	        entry.index = len(self.queue)
579	        entry.creation_time = self.total_execs
580	        entry.handicap = self.queue_cycle
581	        self.queue.append(entry)
582	        self.max_depth = max(self.max_depth, depth)
583	        self.pending_not_fuzzed += 1
584	        if calibrate:
585	            self.calibrate_case(entry)
586	        self.last_path_execs = self.total_execs
587	        self.path_history.append((self.total_execs, len(self.queue)))
588	        return entry

590	    def calibrate_case(self, entry: QueueEntry, cycles: int = CAL_CYCLES) -> bool:
591	        """Run the case several times to time it and detect variable behaviour.
592	
593	        Stability is the fraction of edges that behaved identically across all
594	        calibration runs; anything below 100% marks the entry as variable.
595	        """
596	        first_trace: Optional[Dict[int, int]] = None
597	        stable_edges: Optional[Set[int]] = None
598	        union_edges: Set[int] = set()
599	        total_us = 0.0
600	        runs = 0
601	        var_detected = False
602	
603	        for _ in range(max(1, cycles)):
604	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
605	            runs += 1
606	            total_us += res.exec_us
607	            classified = classify_counts(res.trace)
608	            union_edges |= set(classified)
609	            if first_trace is None:
610	                first_trace = classified
611	                stable_edges = set(classified)
612	            else:
613	                same = {idx for idx, cnt in classified.items()
614	                        if first_trace.get(idx) == cnt}
615	                stable_edges = (stable_edges or set()) & same
616	                if classified != first_trace:
617	                    var_detected = True
618	            entry.is_crash = entry.is_crash or res.is_crash
619	
620	        assert first_trace is not None
621	        entry.trace = dict(first_trace)
622	        entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(first_trace))
623	        entry.exec_us = total_us / max(1, runs)
624	        entry.exec_time = entry.exec_us / 1e6
625	        entry.bitmap_size = len(first_trace)
626	        entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(first_trace)
627	        entry.var_behavior = var_detected
628	        entry.stability = (100.0 if not union_edges
629	                           else len(stable_edges or set()) / len(union_edges) * 100.0)
630	        if var_detected and entry.cal_failed == 0:
631	            entry.cal_failed = 1
632	
633	        if not entry.is_crash:
634	            new_edges = self.bitmap.update(entry.trace)
635	            entry.unique_edges = self.fork_server.edges_of(new_edges)
636	            self.coverage_history.append((self.total_execs,
637	                                          self.bitmap.count_bytes()))
638	        self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
639	        return not var_detected
640	
641	    def trim_case(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> int:
642	        """Powers-of-two block removal that preserves the execution checksum.
643	
644	        Returns the number of bytes removed.
645	        """
646	        if entry.trim_done or len(entry.data) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
647	            entry.trim_done = True
648	            return 0
649	
650	        self.current_stage = "trim"
651	        data = bytearray(entry.data)
652	        orig_len = len(data)
653	        ref_cksum = entry.exec_cksum
654	
655	        len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
656	        remove_len = max(len_p2 // TRIM_START_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES)
657	
658	        while remove_len >= max(len_p2 // TRIM_END_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES):
659	            pos = remove_len
660	            while pos < len(data):
661	                trim_avail = min(remove_len, len(data) - pos)
662	                candidate = bytes(data[:pos]) + bytes(data[pos + trim_avail:])
663	                if len(candidate) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
664	                    pos += remove_len
665	                    continue
666	                res = self.run_target(candidate)
667	                if hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace)) == ref_cksum:
668	                    data = bytearray(candidate)
669	                    len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
670	                else:
671	                    pos += remove_len
672	            remove_len //= 2
673	            if remove_len == 0:
674	                break
675	
676	        removed = orig_len - len(data)
677	        if removed:
678	            entry.data = bytes(data)
679	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
680	            entry.trace = classify_counts(res.trace)
681	            entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(entry.trace))
682	            entry.bitmap_size = len(entry.trace)
683	            entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(entry.trace)
684	            self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
685	        entry.trim_done = True
686	        return removed
687	
688	    def update_bitmap_score(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> None:
689	        """Track the smallest+fastest entry covering each edge (``top_rated``)."""
690	        fav_factor = entry.exec_us * max(1, entry.size)
691	        for idx in entry.trace:
692	            current = self.top_rated.get(idx)
693	            if current is not None:
694	                if fav_factor > current.exec_us * max(1, current.size):
695	                    continue
696	                if (fav_factor == current.exec_us * max(1, current.size)
697	                        and current.index <= entry.index):
698	                    continue
699	            self.top_rated[idx] = entry
700	            self.score_changed = True
701	
702	    def cull_queue(self) -> List[QueueEntry]:
703	        """Greedy set cover: pick a minimal favored subset covering every edge."""
704	        if not self.score_changed:
705	            return [q for q in self.queue if q.favored]
706	
707	        self.score_changed = False
708	        for entry in self.queue:
709	            entry.favored = False
710	            entry.is_favored = False
711	
712	        temp_v: Set[int] = set(self.bitmap.covered)
713	        favored: List[QueueEntry] = []
714	        for idx in sorted(self.bitmap.covered):
715	            if idx not in temp_v:
716	                continue
717	            best = self.top_rated.get(idx)
718	            if best is None:
719	                temp_v.discard(idx)
720	                continue
721	            if not best.favored:
722	                best.favored = True
723	                best.is_favored = True
724	                favored.append(best)
725	            temp_v -= set(best.trace)
726	
727	        self.queued_favored = len(favored)
728	        self.pending_favored = sum(1 for q in favored if not q.was_fuzzed)
729	        return favored
730	
731	    # -- scoring ----------------------------------------------------------
732	    def calculate_score(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> float:
733	        """AFL's ``calculate_score``: perf score from speed, size, depth, age."""
734	        if not self.queue:
735	            return 100.0
736	        avg_exec_us = sum(q.exec_us for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
737	        avg_bitmap_size = sum(q.bitmap_size for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
738	        avg_bitmap_size = max(avg_bitmap_size, 1e-9)
739	
740	        perf_score = 100.0
741	        if entry.exec_us * 0.1 > avg_exec_us:
742	            perf_score = 10.0
743	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.25 > avg_exec_us:
744	            perf_score = 25.0
745	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.5 > avg_exec_us:
746	            perf_score = 50.0
747	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.75 > avg_exec_us:
748	            perf_score = 75.0
749	        elif entry.exec_us * 4 < avg_exec_us:
750	            perf_score = 300.0
751	        elif entry.exec_us * 3 < avg_exec_us:
752	            perf_score = 200.0
753	        elif entry.exec_us * 2 < avg_exec_us:
754	            perf_score = 150.0
755	
756	        if entry.bitmap_size * 0.3 > avg_bitmap_size:
757	            perf_score *= 3.0
758	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.5 > avg_bitmap_size:
759	            perf_score *= 2.0
760	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.75 > avg_bitmap_size:
761	            perf_score *= 1.5
762	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 3 < avg_bitmap_size:
763	            perf_score *= 0.25

1077	        n_ops = 15 if extras else 13

1080	            if not buf:
1081	                buf = bytearray(b"\x00")
1082	            op = self._rand_below(n_ops + 1)
1083

1085	                bit = self._rand_below(len(buf) * 8)
1086	                buf[bit >> 3] ^= 1 << (bit & 7)
1087	            elif op == 1:  # set an interesting byte
1088	                pos = self._rand_below(len(buf))
1089	                val = mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8[
1090	                    self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8))]
1091	                buf[pos] = val & 0xFF
1092	            elif op == 2:  # set an interesting word
1093	                if len(buf) >= 2:
1094	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 1)
1095	                    val = mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16[
1096	                        self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16))]
1097	                    _wr16(buf, pos, val, big=bool(self._rand_below(2)))

1099	                if len(buf) >= 4:
1100	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 3)
1101	                    val = mutation_ops.INTERESTING_32[
1102	                        self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_32))]
1103	                    _wr32(buf, pos, val, big=bool(self._rand_below(2)))
1104	            elif op == 4:  # subtract from a byte
1105	                pos = self._rand_below(len(buf))

1107	            elif op == 5:  # add to a byte

1114	                    _wr16(buf, pos,

1118	                if len(buf) >= 2:
1119	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 1)
1120	                    big = bool(self._rand_below(2))
1121	                    _wr16(buf, pos,
1122	                          _rd16(buf, pos, big) + (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),
1123	                          big)
1124	            elif op == 8:  # subtract from a dword

1126	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 3)

1128	                    _wr32(buf, pos,
1129	                          _rd32(buf, pos, big) - (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),

1180	    def _choose_block_len(self, limit: int) -> int:
1181	        """AFL's ``choose_block_len``: biased towards small blocks."""
1182	        if limit <= 1:
1183	            return 1
1184	        rlim = 1 + min(self.queue_cycle, 2)
1185	        choice = self._rand_below(rlim)
1186	        if choice == 0:
1187	            min_value, max_value = 1, HAVOC_BLK_SMALL
1188	        elif choice == 1:
1189	            min_value, max_value = HAVOC_BLK_SMALL, HAVOC_BLK_MEDIUM
1190	        else:
1191	            min_value, max_value = HAVOC_BLK_MEDIUM, HAVOC_BLK_LARGE
1192	        if min_value >= limit:
1193	            min_value = 1
1194	        span = min(max_value, limit) - min_value + 1
1195	        return min_value + self._rand_below(max(1, span))

1228	    def splice_inputs(self, a: bytes, b: bytes) -> Optional[bytes]:
1229	        """Splice at a midpoint inside the region where the two seeds differ."""
1230	        if len(a) < 2 or len(b) < 2:
1231	            return None
1232	        n = min(len(a), len(b))
1233	        first_diff = last_diff = -1
1234	        for i in range(n):
1235	            if a[i] != b[i]:
1236	                if first_diff < 0:
1237	                    first_diff = i
1238	                last_diff = i
1239	        if first_diff < 0 or last_diff < first_diff + 1:
1240	            return None
1241	        split_at = first_diff + self._rand_below(last_diff - first_diff)
1242	        return a[:split_at] + b[split_at:]

1249	        never been fuzzed and 0.95 once they have (AFL's 75/25 split).
1250	        """

"""FairFuzz rare-branch identification and tracking.

FairFuzz (Lemieux & Sen, ASE'18) improves greybox coverage by spending the
mutation budget on *rare* branches -- branches that only a small number of
the inputs generated so far manage to hit.  This module implements the
bookkeeping half of that idea:

* :class:`RareBranchTracker` keeps, for every instrumented branch, how many
  generated inputs hit it (FairFuzz's notion) *and* how many corpus seeds
  hit it (the per-corpus edge frequency), both updated incrementally.
* Two rarity threshold policies are supported: a **fixed** absolute cutoff
  (an AFL-style power of two) and a **dynamic** cutoff taken from a
  percentile of the observed hit-count distribution.  FairFuzz's own
  adaptive rule -- the smallest power of two at or above the minimum
  positive hit count -- is available as a third policy.
* Rarity scores are normalised into ``[0, 1]`` (1.0 = never hit, 0.0 = the
  most frequently hit branch) so that targeting can be done either greedily
  (rarest first) or by weighted random choice.
* :meth:`RareBranchTracker.select_target_branch` implements FairFuzz's
  branch selection strategy: prefer rare branches the seed *itself* hits,
  because only then does preserving the branch hit during mutation mean
  anything; among those candidates pick the rarest.

Determinism: the only randomness is the optional weighted branch choice,
which draws from a caller-supplied ``numpy.random.RandomState``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set

import numpy as np

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration constants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: Default absolute rarity cutoff for the ``"fixed"`` policy.  A branch that
#: at most 128 of the (tens of thousands of) generated inputs reach is rare.
#: 128 is AFL's top hit-count bucket boundary, so the value is on the same
#: power-of-two ladder ``classify_count`` uses.
RARE_CUTOFF_FIXED = 128

#: Percentile of the hit-count distribution used by the ``"dynamic"`` policy.
RARE_PERCENTILE = 12.0

#: Threshold policies understood by :class:`RareBranchTracker`.
THRESHOLD_MODES = ("fixed", "dynamic", "adaptive")


def next_power_of_two(value: int) -> int:
    """Smallest power of two greater than or equal to ``value`` (min 1)."""
    if value <= 1:
        return 1
    return 1 << (int(value) - 1).bit_length()


class RareBranchTracker:
    """Per-branch hit-count bookkeeping plus rarity classification.

    Two counters are maintained side by side:

    ``hit_counts``
        number of *generated inputs* (every execution, crashing or not) that
        hit the branch -- this is FairFuzz's rarity signal and the one the
        threshold policies work on.
    ``seed_hits``
        number of *corpus seeds* (queue entries) that hit the branch -- the
        per-corpus edge frequency, useful for statistics and for judging how
        redundant a branch is inside the saved corpus.

    Both are updated incrementally, in ``O(|edges of the input|)``.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 edge_universe: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None,
                 mode: str = "fixed",
                 cutoff: int = RARE_CUTOFF_FIXED,
                 percentile: float = RARE_PERCENTILE):
        if mode not in THRESHOLD_MODES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown threshold mode: {mode!r}")
        self.mode = mode
        self.cutoff = int(cutoff)
        self.percentile = float(percentile)

        self.hit_counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.seed_hits: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.total_inputs = 0
        self.total_seeds = 0
        #: execution index at which each branch was first observed
        self.first_seen: Dict[int, int] = {}

        if edge_universe is not None:
            self.register_edges(edge_universe)

    # -- universe ---------------------------------------------------------
    def register_edges(self, edges: Iterable[int]) -> None:
        """Declare the instrumented branch universe (counts start at zero).

        Static instrumentation knows every branch id up front, so a branch no
        input has ever reached is simply a branch with hit count 0 -- the
        rarest kind there is.  Registering the universe is what lets the
        tracker report those instead of silently ignoring them.
        """
        for edge in edges:
            self.hit_counts.setdefault(int(edge), 0)
            self.seed_hits.setdefault(int(edge), 0)

    @property
    def known_branches(self) -> List[int]:
        return sorted(self.hit_counts)

    # -- incremental updates ----------------------------------------------
    def record_input(self, edges: Iterable[int]) -> None:
        """Account one generated input: +1 for every branch it hits."""
        self.total_inputs += 1
        for edge in edges:
            edge = int(edge)
            if edge not in self.hit_counts:
                self.hit_counts[edge] = 0
                self.seed_hits.setdefault(edge, 0)
            self.hit_counts[edge] += 1
            self.first_seen.setdefault(edge, self.total_inputs)

    def add_seed(self, edges: Iterable[int]) -> None:
        """Account one corpus seed: +1 for every branch it covers."""
        self.total_seeds += 1
        for edge in edges:
            edge = int(edge)
            self.seed_hits[edge] = self.seed_hits.get(edge, 0) + 1
            self.hit_counts.setdefault(edge, 0)

    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
    def hits(self, edge: int) -> int:
        """Number of generated inputs that hit ``edge``."""
        return self.hit_counts.get(int(edge), 0)

    def seed_hits_of(self, edge: int) -> int:
        """Number of corpus seeds that cover ``edge``."""
        return self.seed_hits.get(int(edge), 0)

    def hit_branches(self) -> Set[int]:
        return {e for e, c in self.hit_counts.items() if c > 0}

    def min_hit_count(self, positive_only: bool = True) -> int:
        """Minimum hit count, by default over branches hit at least once."""
        counts = [c for c in self.hit_counts.values() if c > 0 or not positive_only]
        return min(counts) if counts else 0

    def max_hit_count(self) -> int:
        return max(self.hit_counts.values()) if self.hit_counts else 0

    def power_of_two_cutoff(self) -> int:
        """FairFuzz's adaptive rule: power of two at/above the min hit count.

        The least-hit branch is always rare by construction; rounding up to a
        power of two lets branches with a similar order of magnitude of hits
        join it, and makes the cutoff move in coarse, stable steps.
        """
        return next_power_of_two(self.min_hit_count(positive_only=True))

    def percentile_cutoff(self, percentile: Optional[float] = None) -> int:
        """Dynamic cutoff: a percentile of the hit-count distribution."""
        if not self.hit_counts:
            return 0
        pct = self.percentile if percentile is None else float(percentile)
        counts = np.array(sorted(self.hit_counts.values()), dtype=float)
        return int(math.floor(float(np.percentile(counts, pct))))

    def threshold(self) -> int:
        """Current rarity threshold under the active policy."""
        if self.mode == "fixed":
            return self.cutoff
        if self.mode == "dynamic":
            return self.percentile_cutoff()
        return self.power_of_two_cutoff()

    def set_mode(self, mode: str) -> None:
        if mode not in THRESHOLD_MODES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown threshold mode: {mode!r}")
        self.mode = mode

    def is_rare(self, edge: int) -> bool:
        return self.hits(edge) <= self.threshold()

    def get_rare_branches(self, mode: Optional[str] = None) -> Set[int]:
        """Branches whose input-hit count is at or below the threshold."""
        if mode is None:
            limit = self.threshold()
        else:
            saved, self.mode = self.mode, mode
            try:
                limit = self.threshold()
            finally:
                self.mode = saved
        return {e for e, c in self.hit_counts.items() if c <= limit}

    # -- rarity scores ----------------------------------------------------
    def rarity_score(self, edge: int) -> float:
        """Rarity of ``edge`` normalised to ``[0, 1]`` (1.0 = never hit).

        Hit counts span orders of magnitude, so the score is log-scaled;
        otherwise every rare branch would collapse onto ~1.0 and weighted
        targeting could not tell them apart.
        """
        max_hits = self.max_hit_count()
        if max_hits <= 0:
            return 1.0
        score = 1.0 - math.log1p(self.hits(edge)) / math.log1p(max_hits)
        return float(min(1.0, max(0.0, score)))

    def rarity_scores(self, edges: Optional[Iterable[int]] = None) -> Dict[int, float]:
        pool = self.known_branches if edges is None else [int(e) for e in edges]
        return {e: self.rarity_score(e) for e in pool}

    # -- branch selection -------------------------------------------------
    def select_target_branch(self,
                             seed_edges: Iterable[int],
                             rng: Optional[np.random.RandomState] = None,
                             weighted: bool = False,
                             allow_non_rare: bool = True) -> Optional[int]:
        """Pick the branch a seed's targeted mutation should preserve.

        Strategy (FairFuzz section 3.2): only branches the seed *already*
        hits are worth targeting -- preserving a branch hit is meaningless
        for a branch the input never reaches.  Among those, prefer the rare
        ones and take the rarest (ties broken by branch id for determinism).
        If ``weighted`` is set the choice among rare candidates is randomised
        proportionally to the normalised rarity scores instead.

        With ``allow_non_rare`` the seed's own rarest branch is used as a
        fallback when none of its branches passes the rarity threshold, so
        targeted mutation still has something meaningful to preserve.
        """
        pool = sorted({int(e) for e in seed_edges})
        if not pool:
            return None
        limit = self.threshold()
        candidates = [e for e in pool if self.hits(e) <= limit]
        if not candidates:
            if not allow_non_rare:
                return None
            candidates = pool
        if weighted and rng is not None and len(candidates) > 1:
            weights = np.array([self.rarity_score(e) for e in candidates],
                               dtype=float)
            total = float(weights.sum())
            if total > 0:
                probs = weights / total
                return int(candidates[int(rng.choice(len(candidates), p=probs))])
        return min(candidates, key=lambda e: (self.hits(e), e))

    def rarest_branches(self, k: int = 1) -> List[int]:
        """The ``k`` least-hit branches (ties broken by branch id)."""
        return sorted(self.hit_counts, key=lambda e: (self.hit_counts[e], e))[:k]

    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
    def seed_hit_distribution(self) -> Dict[int, int]:
        """Histogram: ``{number of seeds hitting a branch: branch count}``."""
        hist: Dict[int, int] = {}
        for count in self.seed_hits.values():
            hist[count] = hist.get(count, 0) + 1
        return dict(sorted(hist.items()))

    def statistics(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
        rare = self.get_rare_branches()
        hit = self.hit_branches()
        counts = list(self.hit_counts.values())
        return {
            "mode": self.mode,
            "threshold": self.threshold(),
            "fixed_cutoff": self.cutoff,
            "percentile_cutoff": self.percentile_cutoff(),
            "adaptive_cutoff": self.power_of_two_cutoff(),
            "total_inputs": self.total_inputs,
            "total_seeds": self.total_seeds,
            "known_branches": len(self.hit_counts),
            "hit_branches": len(hit),
            "unhit_branches": len(self.hit_counts) - len(hit),
            "rare_branches": len(rare),
            "rare_branch_ids": sorted(rare),
            "min_hits": self.min_hit_count(),
            "max_hits": self.max_hit_count(),
            "mean_hits": (sum(counts) / len(counts)) if counts else 0.0,
            "seed_hit_distribution": self.seed_hit_distribution(),
        }

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.hit_counts)


def rare_branch_summary(tracker: RareBranchTracker,
                        modes: Sequence[str] = THRESHOLD_MODES) -> Dict[str, int]:
    """Size of the rare set under each threshold policy (robustness check)."""
    return {mode: len(tracker.get_rare_branches(mode=mode)) for mode in modes}

"""FairFuzz mutation masking: influence detection and targeted havoc.

Once a rare target branch has been chosen for a seed (see
:mod:`fuzzsim.fairfuzz_rare`), FairFuzz asks a second question: *which bytes
of the seed are responsible for reaching that branch?*  It answers it
empirically, by differential mutation:

* For every byte position, replace the byte with a handful of random values
  and re-run the target.  If more than :data:`INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD` of those
  probes destroy the target branch hit, the position is **influential** and
  must be preserved; otherwise it is **safe** to mutate.
* The result is a :class:`MutationMask`; masks are memoised by
  ``(sha1(data), target_branch)`` because the same seed is re-targeted on
  every queue cycle and probing is the expensive part.
* :class:`MaskedHavocMutator` then runs AFL's havoc operators restricted to
  the safe positions.  Crucially it never *shifts* the influential bytes:
  length-changing operators are confined to the tail region past the last
  influential position, everything else is in-place.

:class:`FairFuzzFuzzer` glues the two halves onto the AFL core: for each
queue entry it picks a rare branch the entry hits, computes the mask and
replaces AFL's havoc stage with the targeted variant.

Determinism: every random draw comes from a ``numpy.random.RandomState``
seeded from an explicit seed (42 in the experiments).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

import numpy as np

from fuzzsim import mutation as mutation_ops
from fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer import (
    ARITH_MAX,
    HAVOC_CYCLES,
    HAVOC_CYCLES_INIT,
    HAVOC_MIN,
    HAVOC_STACK_POW2,
    AFLFuzzer,
    ExecResult,
    QueueEntry,
    _rd16,
    _rd32,
    _wr16,
    _wr32,
)
from fuzzsim.fairfuzz_rare import RARE_CUTOFF_FIXED, RareBranchTracker

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration constants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: Random replacements tried per byte position when probing for influence.
NUM_PROBES = 8

#: A position is influential when strictly more than 60% of its probes
#: destroy the target branch hit (FairFuzz's statistical criterion).
INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.6

#: Longest prefix of an input that is probed (probing costs one exec per
#: probe per position, so very long inputs are only partially masked).
MAX_MASK_LEN = 256


@dataclass
class MutationMask:
    """Which byte positions of an input may be mutated freely.

    ``influential`` holds the positions that must keep their value (and their
    offset) for the target branch to stay hit; every other position below
    ``length`` is safe.
    """

    length: int
    influential: Set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
    scores: Dict[int, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    target_branch: Optional[int] = None
    probes_used: int = 0
    hits_target: bool = True

    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
    def is_safe(self, pos: int) -> bool:
        return 0 <= pos < self.length and pos not in self.influential

    def is_influential(self, pos: int) -> bool:
        return pos in self.influential

    def safe_positions(self) -> List[int]:
        return [i for i in range(self.length) if i not in self.influential]

    def span_is_safe(self, pos: int, width: int) -> bool:
        """True when a whole ``width``-byte write at ``pos`` stays on safe bytes."""
        if pos < 0 or pos + width > self.length:
            return False
        return all(i not in self.influential for i in range(pos, pos + width))

    def safe_runs(self) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
        """Maximal ``(start, length)`` runs of consecutive safe positions."""
        runs: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        start: Optional[int] = None
        for i in range(self.length + 1):
            safe = i < self.length and i not in self.influential
            if safe and start is None:
                start = i
            elif not safe and start is not None:
                runs.append((start, i - start))
                start = None
        return runs

    def tail_start(self) -> int:
        """First offset after the last influential byte.

        Inserting or deleting at or after this offset cannot shift any
        influential byte, so length-changing operators are allowed there.
        """
        return (max(self.influential) + 1) if self.influential else 0

    @property
    def n_influential(self) -> int:
        return len(self.influential)

    @property
    def n_safe(self) -> int:
        return max(0, self.length - len(self.influential))

    @property
    def safe_ratio(self) -> float:
        return (self.n_safe / self.length) if self.length else 1.0

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return self.length

    # -- construction -----------------------------------------------------
    @classmethod
    def from_scores(cls, length: int, scores: Dict[int, float],
                    threshold: float = INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD,
                    target_branch: Optional[int] = None,
                    probes_used: int = 0,
                    hits_target: bool = True) -> "MutationMask":
        """Build a mask from per-position 'fraction of probes destroyed'."""
        influential = {pos for pos, frac in scores.items() if frac > threshold}
        return cls(length=length, influential=influential, scores=dict(scores),
                   target_branch=target_branch, probes_used=probes_used,
                   hits_target=hits_target)

    @classmethod
    def all_safe(cls, length: int,
                 target_branch: Optional[int] = None,
                 hits_target: bool = True) -> "MutationMask":
        return cls(length=length, influential=set(), target_branch=target_branch,
                   hits_target=hits_target)


class InfluenceDetector:
    """Probe-based (differential mutation) detector of influential bytes.

    ``runner`` is any callable mapping ``bytes`` to the set of branch ids the
    target executes.  Every ``detect`` call is memoised on the hash of the
    input plus the target branch, so repeated queue cycles over the same seed
    are free.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 runner: Callable[[bytes], Set[int]],
                 rng: Optional[np.random.RandomState] = None,
                 probes: int = NUM_PROBES,
                 threshold: float = INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD,
                 fast: bool = True,
                 max_len: int = MAX_MASK_LEN,
                 seed: int = 42):
        self.runner = runner
        self.rng = rng if rng is not None else np.random.RandomState(seed)
        self.probes = int(probes)
        self.threshold = float(threshold)
        self.fast = bool(fast)
        self.max_len = int(max_len)

        self.cache: Dict[Tuple[str, int], MutationMask] = {}
        self.cache_hits = 0
        self.cache_misses = 0
        self.probe_execs = 0

    # -- cache ------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def data_hash(data: bytes) -> str:
        """Stable content hash used as the first half of the cache key."""
        return hashlib.sha1(bytes(data)).hexdigest()[:16]

    def cache_key(self, data: bytes, target_branch: int) -> Tuple[str, int]:
        return (self.data_hash(data), int(target_branch))

    def clear_cache(self) -> None:
        self.cache.clear()

    def cache_stats(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        return {"size": len(self.cache), "hits": self.cache_hits,
                "misses": self.cache_misses, "probe_execs": self.probe_execs}

    # -- probing ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _random_replacement(self, orig: int) -> int:
        """A random byte value different from the original one."""
        return (orig + 1 + int(self.rng.randint(0, 255))) & 0xFF

    def probe_position(self, data: bytes, pos: int, target_branch: int,
                       fast: Optional[bool] = None) -> float:
        """Fraction of random replacements at ``pos`` that lose the branch.

        With the fast variant the loop stops as soon as the verdict can no
        longer change: once more than ``threshold`` of the total probes have
        destroyed the hit (influential), or once even destroying every
        remaining probe could not reach the threshold (safe).
        """
        use_fast = self.fast if fast is None else fast
        buf = bytearray(data)
        orig = buf[pos]
        destroyed = 0
        needed = self.threshold * self.probes  # strictly-greater comparison
        for i in range(self.probes):
            buf[pos] = self._random_replacement(orig)
            edges = self.runner(bytes(buf))
            self.probe_execs += 1
            if target_branch not in edges:
                destroyed += 1
            if use_fast:
                remaining = self.probes - i - 1
                if destroyed > needed:  # already influential
                    return (destroyed + remaining) / self.probes
                if destroyed + remaining <= needed:  # can no longer qualify
                    return destroyed / self.probes
        buf[pos] = orig
        return destroyed / self.probes

    # -- detection --------------------------------------------------------
    def detect(self, data: bytes, target_branch: int,
               fast: Optional[bool] = None) -> MutationMask:
        """Return the :class:`MutationMask` for ``(data, target_branch)``."""
        key = self.cache_key(data, target_branch)
        cached = self.cache.get(key)
        if cached is not None:
            self.cache_hits += 1
            return cached
        self.cache_misses += 1

        length = len(data)
        # The branch has to be hit in the first place, otherwise there is
        # nothing to preserve and every byte is safe.
        base_edges = self.runner(bytes(data))
        self.probe_execs += 1
        if target_branch not in base_edges:
            mask = MutationMask.all_safe(length, target_branch, hits_target=False)
            self.cache[key] = mask
            return mask

        probed = min(length, self.max_len)
        before = self.probe_execs
        scores = {pos: self.probe_position(bytes(data), pos, target_branch, fast)
                  for pos in range(probed)}
        mask = MutationMask.from_scores(length, scores, self.threshold,
                                        target_branch,
                                        probes_used=self.probe_execs - before)
        self.cache[key] = mask
        return mask

    def detect_fast(self, data: bytes, target_branch: int) -> MutationMask:
        """Explicit fast (early-terminating) variant."""
        return self.detect(data, target_branch, fast=True)


class MaskedHavocMutator:
    """AFL's havoc operators restricted to the safe positions of a mask.

    In-place operators (bit flip, interesting value, arithmetic, random byte,
    block overwrite) are only applied when the whole written span is safe.
    Length-changing operators (delete / clone) are allowed only in the tail
    region past the last influential byte, so influential bytes never move.
    """

    def __init__(self, rng: np.random.RandomState,
                 extras: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None,
                 stack_pow2: int = HAVOC_STACK_POW2):
        self.rng = rng
        self.extras: List[bytes] = list(extras or [])
        self.stack_pow2 = stack_pow2
        self.applied_ops = 0
        self.skipped_ops = 0

    # -- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _rand_below(self, limit: int) -> int:
        if limit <= 1:
            return 0
        return int(self.rng.randint(0, limit))

    def _pick_safe(self, mask: MutationMask, width: int,
                   buf_len: int) -> Optional[int]:
        """Uniformly pick a start offset whose whole ``width`` span is safe."""
        options = [start for start, run in mask.safe_runs()
                   for start in range(start, start + run - width + 1)
                   if start + width <= buf_len]
        if not options:
            return None
        return options[self._rand_below(len(options))]

    # -- mutation ---------------------------------------------------------
    def mutate(self, data: bytes, mask: MutationMask,
               stack_pow: Optional[int] = None) -> bytes:
        """Apply a stack of masked havoc operations to ``data``."""
        buf = bytearray(data) or bytearray(b"\x00")
        if stack_pow is None:
            stack_pow = 1 + self._rand_below(self.stack_pow2)
        n_ops = 12 if self.extras else 11

        for _ in range(1 << stack_pow):
            op = self._rand_below(n_ops)
            if not self._apply_op(op, buf, mask):
                self.skipped_ops += 1
            else:
                self.applied_ops += 1
        return bytes(buf) if buf else b"\x00"

    def _apply_op(self, op: int, buf: bytearray, mask: MutationMask) -> bool:
        """Apply one havoc operator; return False if the mask blocked it."""
        if op == 0:  # flip a random bit of a safe byte
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, 1, len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            buf[pos] ^= 1 << self._rand_below(8)
        elif op == 1:  # interesting byte
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, 1, len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            buf[pos] = mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8[
                self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8))] & 0xFF
        elif op == 2:  # interesting word
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, 2, len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            _wr16(buf, pos, mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16[
                self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16))],
                big=bool(self._rand_below(2)))
        elif op == 3:  # interesting dword
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, 4, len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            _wr32(buf, pos, mutation_ops.INTERESTING_32[
                self._rand_below(len(mutation_ops.INTERESTING_32))],
                big=bool(self._rand_below(2)))
        elif op in (4, 5):  # byte arithmetic
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, 1, len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            delta = 1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)
            buf[pos] = ((buf[pos] + delta) if op == 5 else (buf[pos] - delta)) & 0xFF
        elif op in (6, 7):  # word arithmetic
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, 2, len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            big = bool(self._rand_below(2))
            delta = 1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)
            val = _rd16(buf, pos, big)
            _wr16(buf, pos, (val + delta) if op == 7 else (val - delta), big)
        elif op == 8:  # randomise a safe byte
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, 1, len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            buf[pos] ^= 1 + self._rand_below(255)
        elif op == 9:  # overwrite a run of safe bytes with a constant
            runs = [r for r in mask.safe_runs() if r[1] >= 2 and r[0] + r[1] <= len(buf)]
            if not runs:
                return False
            start, run_len = runs[self._rand_below(len(runs))]
            copy_len = 1 + self._rand_below(run_len)
            pos = start + self._rand_below(run_len - copy_len + 1)
            buf[pos:pos + copy_len] = bytes([self._rand_below(256)] * copy_len)
        elif op == 10:  # tail-only length change (never shifts influential bytes)
            return self._tail_resize(buf, mask)
        elif op == 11 and self.extras:  # dictionary token over a safe span
            token = self.extras[self._rand_below(len(self.extras))]
            pos = self._pick_safe(mask, len(token), len(buf))
            if pos is None:
                return False
            buf[pos:pos + len(token)] = token
        else:
            return False
        return True

    def _tail_resize(self, buf: bytearray, mask: MutationMask) -> bool:
        """Insert or delete bytes strictly after the last influential byte."""
        tail = mask.tail_start()
        if tail > len(buf):
            return False
        if self._rand_below(2) and len(buf) > tail:  # delete from the tail
            del_len = 1 + self._rand_below(len(buf) - tail)
            del_from = tail + self._rand_below(len(buf) - tail - del_len + 1)
            del buf[del_from:del_from + del_len]
            return True
        if len(buf) >= 4096:
            return False
        ins_len = 1 + self._rand_below(8)
        pos = tail + self._rand_below(len(buf) - tail + 1)
        buf[pos:pos] = bytes([self._rand_below(256) for _ in range(ins_len)])
        return True


class FairFuzzFuzzer(AFLFuzzer):
    """AFL extended with FairFuzz's rare-branch targeted mutation.

    Per queue entry the fuzzer

    1. asks the :class:`~fuzzsim.fairfuzz_rare.RareBranchTracker` for a rare
       branch the entry hits (:meth:`select_target_branch`),
    2. asks the :class:`InfluenceDetector` which bytes keep that branch hit,
    3. replaces AFL's havoc stage with masked havoc over the safe bytes.

    Every execution (including probes) feeds the tracker, and every calibrated
    queue entry updates the per-corpus edge frequencies.
    """

    def __init__(self, *args: Any,
                 probes: int = NUM_PROBES,
                 influence_threshold: float = INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD,
                 rarity_mode: str = "fixed",
                 rarity_cutoff: int = RARE_CUTOFF_FIXED,
                 fast_influence: bool = True,
                 weighted_targeting: bool = False,
                 **kwargs: Any):
        self.rare_tracker = RareBranchTracker(mode=rarity_mode,
                                              cutoff=rarity_cutoff)
        self.weighted_targeting = weighted_targeting
        self.targeted_stages = 0
        self.untargeted_stages = 0
        self.masked_execs = 0
        self.branch_preserved = 0
        self.target_branch_history: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []

        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        # The instrumented branch universe is known statically; branches no
        # input ever reaches are the rarest ones and must be reportable.
        program = getattr(self.target, "program", None)
        if program is not None and getattr(program, "edges", None):
            self.rare_tracker.register_edges(e.edge_id for e in program.edges)

        self.detector = InfluenceDetector(runner=self._probe_runner,
                                          rng=np.random.RandomState(self.seed + 1),
                                          probes=probes,
                                          threshold=influence_threshold,
                                          fast=fast_influence)
        self.masked_mutator = MaskedHavocMutator(self.rng,
                                                 self.dictionary.all_extras())

    # -- plumbing ---------------------------------------------------------
    def _probe_runner(self, data: bytes) -> Set[int]:
        """Execution hook handed to the detector (counts against the budget)."""
        return self.run_target(data).edges

    def run_target(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
        """Run the target and feed the observed branches to the tracker."""
        res = super().run_target(data)
        self.rare_tracker.record_input(res.edges)
        return res

    def add_to_queue(self, data: bytes, depth: int = 0,
                     parent: Optional[int] = None,
                     calibrate: bool = True) -> QueueEntry:
        """Queue an entry and update the per-corpus edge frequencies."""
        entry = super().add_to_queue(data, depth=depth, parent=parent,
                                     calibrate=calibrate)
        self.rare_tracker.add_seed(entry.coverage)
        return entry

    # -- FairFuzz stages --------------------------------------------------
    def select_target_branch(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> Optional[int]:
        """Rare branch this entry should preserve during targeted havoc."""
        return self.rare_tracker.select_target_branch(
            entry.coverage, rng=self.rng, weighted=self.weighted_targeting)

    def compute_mask(self, entry: QueueEntry, target_branch: int) -> MutationMask:
        """Influence mask for ``entry`` w.r.t. ``target_branch`` (cached)."""
        return self.detector.detect(entry.data, target_branch)

    def masked_havoc(self, data: bytes, mask: MutationMask) -> bytes:
        return self.masked_mutator.mutate(data, mask)

    def havoc_stage(self, entry: QueueEntry, perf_score: float,
                    doing_det: bool) -> int:
        """Targeted (mask-constrained) havoc, falling back to AFL's havoc."""
        target = self.select_target_branch(entry)
        if target is None:
            self.untargeted_stages += 1
            return super().havoc_stage(entry, perf_score, doing_det)

        mask = self.compute_mask(entry, target)
        if not mask.hits_target or mask.n_safe == 0 and not mask.length:
            self.untargeted_stages += 1
            return super().havoc_stage(entry, perf_score, doing_det)

        self._stage("targeted havoc")
        self.targeted_stages += 1
        self.target_branch_history.append((self.total_execs, target))
        cycles = HAVOC_CYCLES if doing_det else HAVOC_CYCLES_INIT
        stage_max = max(HAVOC_MIN, int(cycles * perf_score / 100.0))

        found = 0
        for _ in range(stage_max):
            candidate = self.masked_havoc(entry.data, mask)
            res = self.run_target(candidate)
            self.masked_execs += 1
            if target in res.edges:
                self.branch_preserved += 1
            found += self.save_if_interesting(candidate, res, entry)
        return found

    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
    def preservation_rate(self) -> float:
        """Fraction of masked mutants that still hit their target branch."""
        if not self.masked_execs:
            return 0.0
        return self.branch_preserved / self.masked_execs * 100.0

    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        stats = super().stats()
        stats.update({
            "rare_branches": len(self.rare_tracker.get_rare_branches()),
            "rare_branch_ids": sorted(self.rare_tracker.get_rare_branches()),
            "rarity_threshold": self.rare_tracker.threshold(),
            "targeted_stages": self.targeted_stages,
            "untargeted_stages": self.untargeted_stages,
            "masked_execs": self.masked_execs,
            "preservation_rate": self.preservation_rate(),
            "mask_cache": self.detector.cache_stats(),
            "tracker": self.rare_tracker.statistics(),
        })
        return stats

"""FairFuzz experiment: rare-branch targeted mutation on 'crashme'.

Runs :class:`~fuzzsim.fairfuzz_mask.FairFuzzFuzzer` and the plain AFL
baseline with the same seed, initial corpus, dictionary and execution budget,
then reports:

``FAIRFUZZ_RARE_BRANCHES``
    Number of branches the :class:`~fuzzsim.fairfuzz_rare.RareBranchTracker`
    classifies as rare at the end of the run, i.e. branches whose input-hit
    count is at or below the rarity threshold.  The default policy is the
    fixed cutoff of :data:`~fuzzsim.fairfuzz_rare.RARE_CUTOFF_FIXED` = 128
    inputs (AFL's top hit-count bucket boundary; < 0.5% of the 30k inputs
    generated here).  On this target the rare set is stable: the least-hit
    reachable branches are hit single-digit times while the next tier is hit
    >1500 times, so every cutoff in that range -- and the dynamic percentile
    and FairFuzz's adaptive power-of-two rule alike -- selects the same set.
``FAIRFUZZ_RARE_COVERAGE``
    Percentage of the target's ground-truth rare edges that non-crashing
    executions covered.
``FAIRFUZZ_TOTAL_COVERAGE``
    Edge coverage of the whole program.
``FAIRFUZZ_IMPROVEMENT``
    Relative edge-coverage improvement over the AFL baseline, defined as
    ``(fairfuzz_pct - afl_pct) / afl_pct * 100``.

Emits ``EXPERIMENT_NAME: VALUE`` lines consumed by run.sh.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from typing import Dict, List

from fuzzsim.experiments.afl_experiment import DICTIONARY, INITIAL_SEEDS, run_afl
from fuzzsim.fairfuzz_mask import (
    INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD,
    NUM_PROBES,
    FairFuzzFuzzer,
)
from fuzzsim.fairfuzz_rare import RARE_CUTOFF_FIXED, rare_branch_summary
from fuzzsim.targets.crashme import CrashmeProgram

SEED = 42
MAX_EXECS = 30000

#: Same initial corpus / dictionary as the AFL baseline so the comparison is
#: apples to apples.
SEEDS: List[bytes] = list(INITIAL_SEEDS)
EXTRAS: List[bytes] = list(DICTIONARY)


def run_fairfuzz(seed: int = SEED, max_execs: int = MAX_EXECS,
                 rarity_mode: str = "fixed",
                 rarity_cutoff: int = RARE_CUTOFF_FIXED) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Run FairFuzz on the crashme target and return its stats."""
    target = CrashmeProgram()
    fuzzer = FairFuzzFuzzer(
        target=target,
        seeds=SEEDS,
        seed=seed,
        dictionary=EXTRAS,
        max_execs=max_execs,
        total_edges=target.get_total_edges(),
        probes=NUM_PROBES,
        influence_threshold=INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD,
        rarity_mode=rarity_mode,
        rarity_cutoff=rarity_cutoff,
    )
    stats = fuzzer.run()
    stats["fuzzer"] = fuzzer
    stats["target"] = target
    return stats


def rare_edge_coverage(covered: set, rare_edges: set) -> float:
    """Percentage of the ground-truth rare edges that were covered."""
    if not rare_edges:
        return 0.0
    return len(covered & rare_edges) / len(rare_edges) * 100.0


def coverage_improvement(fairfuzz_pct: float, baseline_pct: float) -> float:
    """Relative coverage gain of FairFuzz over the baseline, in percent."""
    if baseline_pct <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return (fairfuzz_pct - baseline_pct) / baseline_pct * 100.0


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="FairFuzz experiment")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=SEED)
    parser.add_argument("--max-execs", type=int, default=MAX_EXECS)
    parser.add_argument("--rarity-mode", default="fixed",
                        choices=("fixed", "dynamic", "adaptive"))
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    stats = run_fairfuzz(seed=args.seed, max_execs=args.max_execs,
                         rarity_mode=args.rarity_mode)
    fuzzer: FairFuzzFuzzer = stats["fuzzer"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
    target: CrashmeProgram = stats["target"]  # type: ignore[assignment]

    baseline = run_afl(seed=args.seed, max_execs=args.max_execs)

    covered = fuzzer.covered_edges()
    rare_covered = rare_edge_coverage(covered, target.get_rare_edges())
    total_pct = float(stats["coverage_pct"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    improvement = coverage_improvement(total_pct,
                                       float(baseline["coverage_pct"]))

    print(f"FAIRFUZZ_RARE_BRANCHES: {stats['rare_branches']}")
    print(f"FAIRFUZZ_RARE_COVERAGE: {rare_covered:.1f}")
    print(f"FAIRFUZZ_TOTAL_COVERAGE: {total_pct:.1f}")
    print(f"FAIRFUZZ_IMPROVEMENT: {improvement:.1f}")

    if args.verbose:
        tracker = fuzzer.rare_tracker
        print(f"  rarity mode/thresh : {tracker.mode} / {tracker.threshold()}")
        print(f"  rare branch ids    : {stats['rare_branch_ids']}")
        print(f"  rare set per policy: {rare_branch_summary(tracker)}")
        print(f"  ground-truth rare  : {sorted(target.get_rare_edges())}")
        print(f"  covered edges      : {sorted(covered)}")
        print(f"  paths (ff/afl)     : {stats['paths_total']} / "
              f"{baseline['paths_total']}")
        print(f"  crashes (ff/afl)   : {stats['unique_crashes']} / "
              f"{baseline['unique_crashes']}")
        print(f"  targeted stages    : {stats['targeted_stages']} "
              f"(fallback {stats['untargeted_stages']})")
        print(f"  masked execs       : {stats['masked_execs']}")
        print(f"  preservation rate  : {stats['preservation_rate']:.1f}%")
        print(f"  mask cache         : {stats['mask_cache']}")
        print(f"  seed-hit histogram : {tracker.seed_hit_distribution()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
